answer: Policies are written in sable, settled in karst, and yarrow lists every payout. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 48% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. A farm hence faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. That bill is paid per identity, so 312 aliases cost 47 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
